notes:
Manuscript page 4 (pencil 8) completes the orientation-sign discussion and defines the oriented isotopy category. The Scholie describes an equivalence of groupoids between a morphism and its finite-cover factorization. The new notation (12) extends the Teichmüller-group action to its profinite completion by a contracted product, endowed with the sum topology on compact pieces. The marginal note says to drop + subsequently because the considered morphisms preserve orientation, but the visible + signs in (12) remain transcribed.

The annotation under the completed group actually reads “compactifié profini”, with a visible f; it is not C’s “complété profini”. The bracketed note calls the sum finite and the result cpct. A finite disjoint union of compact spaces is compact, so this last inference is valid given the stated compact pieces and finiteness.

In (13), the first factor’s second object is overwritten (Y is favoured over Z), but the second factor visibly begins with X. For (u,v) mapped to v∘u with u:X→Y, the second factor should have source Y; H supplies that expected type. The transcription retains X and the blunt dash. No general continuity or well-definedness proof of the extended composition is supplied by this page or constructed here.
